original_text: User(s) follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of gestures to “win” the game

attribute_scores.rationale: Terms like 'win' the game are subjective and undefined in the context of system requirements without specific scoring or state-transition criteria.
Lacks specific conditions for what happens when instructions are ignored, gestures are unrecognized, or game states are triggered.
Terminology aligns generally with the system domain, though 'User(s)' introduces slight stylistic variance.
Violates standard syntactic structure; it uses descriptive present tense ('follow', 'must make use') instead of the mandatory normative modal verb 'shall'.
Technically feasible within a gesture recognition system context, though phrased more like a user manual instruction than a system requirement.
Combines two distinct requirements into one statement: following on-screen instructions and making use of gestures to win.
Difficult to test objectively due to the vague definition of 'win' the game and the unconstrained nature of 'on-screen instructions'.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: User(s) follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of
shortcomings.explanation: The requirement fails to use the mandatory normative modal verb 'shall' required by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 for binding requirements.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of gestures
shortcomings.explanation: The statement couples two separate behaviors (interacting with on-screen instructions and performing gestures), violating the rule of singularity.
The term 'win' is subjective and lacks precise, testable criteria defining the precise conditions required to achieve a win state.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: This requirement relates to the functional interaction flow of the FROG gesture recognition system, describing how an end user participates in a game-like scenario using on-screen instructions and physical gestures tracked by the sensor system.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: User(s) follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of
evaluations.context_reasoning: The applicable standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 explicitly dictates the use of mandatory normative modal verbs ('shall') for binding system requirements. The current text uses descriptive/non-normative phrasing ('must make use of') instead of the strict imperative 'shall', which is a valid and justified conformance defect.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of gestures
evaluations.context_reasoning: The flagging of singularity is overly pedantic. Reading instructions and executing the corresponding gestures are inextricably linked parts of a single unified user interaction loop within a gesture recognition game, rather than two distinct functional requirements that need independent allocation or tracking.

The term 'win' is enclosed in quotes and lacks clear, measurable boundary conditions, score thresholds, or completion states within the text or general SRS glossary. Without explicit success criteria, testing this requirement is ambiguous and subjective.

layer2.reasoning_summary: Evaluated three candidate defects against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 standards and SRS context. DEF-1 is justified because the requirement lacks the mandatory modal 'shall'. DEF-2 is discarded as a false positive because following instructions and performing gestures form a single cohesive user interaction sequence for the game. DEF-3 is justified as 'win' is indeed subjective and lacks testable success criteria within this specific requirement.

layer3.original_text: User(s) follow the on-screen instructions and must make use of gestures to “win” the game
layer3.refined_text: When following on-screen instructions, the FROG system shall require user(s) to execute gestures to achieve the defined game completion condition.
changes_made: Applied EARS event-driven syntax ('When..., the FROG system shall...') to incorporate the mandatory modal verb 'shall' per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.
Replaced the subjective term 'win' with the precise, testable phrase 'achieve the defined game completion condition' to eliminate ambiguity while preserving the original intent.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The refinement strictly preserves the core logic that users must interact via gestures based on on-screen instructions to successfully complete the game. It only introduces the mandatory 'shall' normative phrasing and clarifies the subjective win state into a testable completion condition without altering the system scope or user workflow.

checks.observations: Successfully replaced non-compliant phrasing with the mandatory 'shall' modal verb and resolved the subjective 'win' term by referencing a defined game completion condition.
The refinement avoids introducing vague adjectives, subjective descriptors, or fuzzy bounds. 'Defined game completion condition' points to system specifications appropriately.
No unauthorized protocols, specific third-party APIs, or out-of-scope technical constraints were invented in the refinement.
The core business logic requiring users to perform gestures per on-screen instructions for game success remains completely intact.
Adheres to EARS event-driven syntax ('When..., the FROG system shall...') and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 standards.

layer4.critique_and_feedback: The proposed refinement successfully addresses all identified defects from Layer 2. It introduces the mandatory modal verb 'shall' using standard EARS format, and properly replaces the subjective term 'win' with a testable, objective phrase ('achieve the defined game completion condition') without over-specifying implementation details or altering the functional scope of the system.
